report.finding: The model is correct and the integrator is fine. This is a linear ODE dS1/dt = vo - k1*S1 with time constant 1/k1 = 50. Approach to steady state (analytically S1(t) = (vo/k1)(1-exp(-k1 t)), steady state = vo/k1 = 50) requires several hundred time units to visibly flatten. The user simulated only to t=10, i.e. 0.2 time constants, where S1 is still at ~18% of its final value and necessarily looks like it's "still climbing" - because it is, just slowly. Tightening tolerances does nothing because there's no numerical error; the trajectory is smooth and well resolved even at loose tolerance.
report.evidence: Re-simulating the unmodified model from t=0 to t=300 gives S1(300)=49.876, converging cleanly to the analytic steady state vo/k1 = 1/0.02 = 50. The original run to t=10 only reaches S1=9.06, consistent with (vo/k1)(1-exp(-0.02*10))=9.06. No tolerance or solver change affects this - the dynamics are just slow (time constant 50 time units).

recommended_changes.why: The system's relaxation time is 1/k1=50; simulating only to t=10 shows less than one-fifth of a time constant, so it appears to be climbing indefinitely. Extending the run to ~300 time units (6 time constants) shows clear convergence to the steady state S1=vo/k1=50.
